data.passage:
Mr. Vincent wants to plan a celebration for his whole class of first-grade students. It will be a special occasion for the end of the school year!

The students have come a long way since the first day of school. Back then, half of the students did not use capitalization in their compositions. Today, they know to use a capital for the first word in a sentence and with a specific name, place, or thing. The students have finished hundreds of books in total, putting their well-developed reading skills to the test.

On top of all of that, the students have their addition and subtraction facts down pat in math. They are also good at communication, active discussions, asking questions that make sense, and using their imaginations to solve tricky problems. Mr. Vincent is so pleased with their progress and, best of all, the kids are pleased with themselves.

For the big celebration, Mr. Vincent will get a bunch of decorations, vanilla cupcakes, and plenty of drinks. He plans to have music, crafts, and games as well. Mr. Vincent is envisioning a great time for all!

Mr. Vincent thinks that one student’s suggestion to extend invitations to the school administration and the students’ families is great. He hopes the celebration will be a hit with all who attend. He is so glad that he will be able to demonstrate to his students how accomplished they are before they set off on vacation - and then on to second grade!

questions.question: What special occasion is the celebration for?
What capitalization skill do the students now know?
What academic areas besides reading are described as strengths?
Why is Mr. Vincent pleased with the students?
What items will Mr. Vincent get for the celebration?
What activities does he plan to include?
Whose suggestion does Mr. Vincent think is great?
Why does he want the celebration to include the school administration and families?
What transition will follow the celebration?
